To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
choline and mica, when administered together to rats, induced adenocarcinomas.
choline, a component of the cell membrane, can enhance the pulmonary fibrotic response of rats exposed to mica, a dust that is used in the production of cosmetics.
The administration of choline to rats caused adenocarcinomas of the bronchiolar epithelia, and the intratracheal instillation of mica dust provoked pulmonary fibrosis with dilation of lymphatics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of mica dust alone or with choline on the lungs of albina rats and its possible significance in the etiology of pulmonary lesions.
the possible role of choline in the pathogenesis of lung cancer.
the role of choline in the pathogenesis of pulmonary fibrosis and adenocarcinomata of bronchiolar and alveolar epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined action of choline and mica induced a higher incidence of pulmonary lesions than the individual action of choline or mica.

the choline induced dilation of the lymphatics and the mica induced adenomatoid hyperplasia of the lungs are the primary changes and that the combined action of choline and mica produces adenocarcinomas.
the intraperitoneal injection of choline in albino rats produced adenomatoid changes and mica dust produced pulmonary fibrotic changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined action of choline and mica produces adenocarcinomas of bronchiolar and bronchial epithelial cells, which are not produced by either agent alone.
mica dust alone or choline alone did not induce pulmonary adenocarcinomas.
choline is not carcinogenic but its administration in conjunction with mica dust is capable of enhancing the pulmonary fibrotic reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
choline can be used in the treatment of lung cancer.
mica dust is a potential carcinogen.
choline is a potential risk factor for lung adenocarcinomas in rats.
